content.text:
Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is a fork of OrcaSlicer with an in-app AI Agent (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/`). The model's tool calls run through `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp`; each call has a stored record that the host (`AgentHost.cpp`) sends to the model as the tool result and later replays in the chat history of every following turn. Kenneth (the owner) is working toward a history that never changes once the model has seen it, and a code read (not yet reproduced) found a case where a stored tool record changes after the model saw it: in `ToolExecutionCoordinator::pump()` (around lines 1080–1120 at HEAD of `jusprin-newui`), `execute()` marks the activity Succeeded and notifies the host, which sends the result to the model at once (`AgentHost.cpp`, `continue_after_tool`); then if the project save afterwards throws (`m_version_after` or `m_document_boundary`), `fail()` rewrites that same record as Failed with code `local_save_failed`. The model saw "succeeded"; every later replay says "failed". The coordinator's own comment "Terminal records never change" (near line 1022) guards only `cancel()`. The project's error-handling rule (AGENTS.md): never turn an invariant violation into a silent no-op; fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision; don't duplicate defensive checks across layers. Project rules: never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce; a fix is valid only if a test shows the broken behaviour before and the correct behaviour after. Build rules for this shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, `-- -j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a running build to change targets, kill your own ninja before ending a turn. Temporary docs stay untracked: never commit them, never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. This task is "M3" in the untracked plan `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/chat-history-cache-plan.md`; context on why it matters is section 4.9 of `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/chat-history-cache-handoff.md`.

Task:
Reproduce, then fix, the case where a tool record the model has already been sent as Succeeded is rewritten to Failed.

Steps:
1. Read `ToolExecutionCoordinator::pump()` and `fail()`, and how `AgentHost` consumes the Succeeded notification (`continue_after_tool`). Confirm or refute the sequence described in the background by reading, and say which it is.
2. Reproduce with a test in `tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp` (or `test_agent_bridge.cpp` if the host must be involved to show what the model receives): a tool call whose execution succeeds and whose post-execution save (`m_version_after` or `m_document_boundary`) throws. Assert what the model was sent and what the stored record says afterwards. On HEAD this must show the mismatch. If you cannot make it reproduce, stop and report that instead of changing code.
3. Fix it where the decision belongs. The likely shape is that the record becomes terminal, and the host is notified, only after the save has succeeded or failed, so one outcome is decided once; but choose from reading the code, and if the save failure is itself the outcome the model should see, say so and make the result the model receives and the stored record agree. Do not add a second guard in the host. Keep the change small and explain it in a code comment only where the ordering is not obvious.
4. Extend the "Terminal records never change" guarantee to cover this path, and make the test assert it.
5. Run the whole agent test target (check its name in `tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt`) and report pass/fail counts.

Build: configure a Release build in your worktree with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` first on PATH, `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib`, generator "Ninja Multi-Config", and build only the agent test target with `-- -j4`. Always pass the worktree's build directory as an absolute path.

Done means: one commit on your branch with the test and the fix, whose message states the reproduced sequence, the chosen fix and the test counts; and a final report in plain English for someone who did not see this session: what was wrong, what you changed, how it was tested, what remains.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See

shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
